gpu-10m.note: One entry per engine SHAPE. With no mini batch the whole request is the call, so a shape is a ROW COUNT and one cache directory serves every session count at that row count -- a session count loads more copies of the same engine, it does not change the engine. Primed on the SAME WIRE the cells use, so no cell can pay for a TensorRT build inside its warm-up. build_seconds is a 20 s trickle against a cold cache, so it carries the TensorRT engine build; cached_seconds is the same trickle against a FRESH server that loaded the cache. The gap is the cost every cell would otherwise have paid inside its warm-up.

neuron-10m.note: One entry per NEFF SHAPE, which is the mini batch: a NEFF's leading dimension is FIXED, so every mini-batch size in the grid is a separate compile and a cell can only run a shape that exists. `source` is `compiled` when this lane built it and `s3-cache` when an earlier lane did -- a NEFF is a pure function of the seeded architecture, the target parameter count and the batch size, so reusing one is reusing the same bytes, which the SHA-256 records. `load_proof_seconds` is a 20 s trickle of exactly `mini_batch` rows served by a FRESH server, so a NEFF that loads but cannot serve is found here rather than inside a cell's warm-up.

metadata.compile_route_note: torch_neuronx.trace compiles the parameters in as CONSTANTS, so the NEFF takes one input -- the [batch, width] feature tensor -- which is the contract hushar's backend serves. The torch-neuronx 2.14 dynamo backend was evaluated and cannot replace it: it writes no model NEFF to disk, and the graph it lowers is stateless, so a NEFF built from its StableHLO takes weights as inputs and hushar refuses it. Same route as config-sweep-neuron-trn1-10M-50M.
